root_idea.summary: The root centers on clothing or covering something by placing an outer layer upon it.
root_idea.development: The clothing image extends to covering land with vegetation and to figurative coverings such as dust, while the Quranic forms attest clothing people and covering bones with flesh.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with an independently supported clothing and covering use.
Quran-attested nominal form with the lexical meaning clothing or garment.

senses.definition: To clothe or cover someone or something by putting an outer layer upon it; to provide clothing for people or to cover bones with flesh.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive. In the Quranic usages, the covering may be ordinary clothing supplied to people or flesh placed over bones in an anatomical construction.
In the Quranic contexts, clothing is understood as clothing worn or supplied for the persons concerned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To invest or furnish someone with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction كَسَوْتُهُ سَيْفًا, meaning to equip or invest him with a sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment, especially a single-piece wrapper or wrapping cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The garment is properly described as a single piece rather than one cut and sewn, though it could sometimes be sewn in the manner of an ʿabāʾah.
A reported figurative use in the contrast ذُو كِسَاءٍ versus ذُو بُرْدٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fall upon the back of one's neck.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participial adjective describing one who has clothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become clothed or covered, as land with vegetation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive derived construction; the attested example describes land covered with vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thin covering or film over milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A poetic expression is interpreted as referring to milk once its thin skin has formed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The backs or rear parts of horses, in a poetic idiom.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In على أَكْسَاءِ خَيْلٍ; the expression is explained through dust clothing the animals.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The attested sword-investment construction is represented as a Classical meaning.
Single-piece wrapper details and the ذُو كِسَاءٍ idiom are represented.
The idiom for falling on the back of the neck is represented.
The adjective meaning having clothing is represented.

cautions: كِسَاءٌ, the classical garment or wrapper, is lexically distinct from the Quranic nominal citation form كِسْوَةٌ, although both belong to the clothing field.
The rare poetic and idiomatic uses are broader Classical Arabic evidence and are not presented as additional Quranic senses.
